Source: FEC filings, via the tracker dataset. Data as of 2026-11-22.

These are the 535 seats of the incoming 120th Congress — 435 in the House, 100 in the Senate. Each dot is one seat.

First, the party split — Democrats in one block, Republicans in one block, in each chamber. House: 261 Democrats, 173 Republicans. Senate: 53 Democrats, 45 Republicans, 2 independents.

Now who the rules flag — any AIPAC direct dollar or UDP benefit dollar since their last election. House: 241 of 435 seats. Senate: 61 of 100. Flagged members sit at the head of their party's block, in the lighter tint of their own party's colour. Under the Balanced tolerance (corporate PAC over $100k and over 5% of receipts), 361 of the incoming 535 count as dirty. How we flagged members.

Total accepted is individual contributions + corporate PAC + AIPAC direct. UDP benefit is spending about a race, never money given to the campaign, so it is not in these bars.

Source: FEC filings, via the tracker dataset. Data as of 2026-11-22.

Where the money comes from. Start with the AIPAC PAC: $27.8M to House campaigns since their last election, $15.8M to Senate campaigns — direct contributions, earmarked checks included.

Add corporate PACs: $103.8M in the House, $66.2M in the Senate. Together with AIPAC, that is $131.6M House and $82M Senate from PACs.

And individuals — the rest, and most of it: $807.4M House, $2.1B Senate. Individual contributions are not dirty money. Total accepted since their last election: $939M House, $2.2B Senate.

The money is real. The question is what it buys.

The zoom-out shows incoming members of the chamber the member ran for only. The subject’s bar sits above theirs, in the accent colour, because the subject is not one of them.

Source: FEC filings, via the tracker dataset. Data as of 2026-11-22.

Haley M. Stevens took $31.4M in dirty money in 2026 — the most of anyone in the dataset — almost all of it UDP benefit: $30.6M spent on the 2026 Senate race, against $11.3M raised from individuals. She is not returning to Congress.

It was not always like this. Dirty money by election: $30K in 2018, $470K in 2020, $5.4M in 2022, $656K in 2024, $31.4M in 2026, the Senate race.

Zoom back out to the Senate. The incoming member who took the most dirty money, Jacky Rosen, took $2.9M — Stevens took more than 10 times that. The Senate median is $663K.
